Maya R.: Heads up — we started seeing org-level rate rejections spike at ~02:12UTC, but the metering pipeline lag shows a 45s writeback delay. rejections don't line up with real usage overflow.
Sanjay K.: Hmm, did enforcer switch to the new prefix-lease routing yesterday? :thinking_face:
Maya R.: Yeah, deploy went out at 01:50. Logs show enforcer reading counters from realtime cache, then rejecting with this: 
```
[2026-03-17T02:12:08Z] enforcer WARN org=acme corp_key=sk-*** rejections=12 reason=quota_exceeded tokens_used=10234 cached_ts=1712349987
```
Ellie (eng-platform): Looks like cached_ts is older than ledger writeback. meter-ingest writes to kafka partition 4, but the accumulator that writes to redis is behind during bursts.
Adrian L.: So enforcement is using stale state and over-rejecting? Could be the prefix routing combined with per-key burst windows.
Kevin T.: We saw similar but the other direction last month (under-throttling) when replay caused duplicate credits. We need a deterministic reconciliation.
Maya R.: Proposal: add a configurable "staleness_grace_ms" to enforcer where if counter age > grace -> use shadow enforcement or extend burst allowance for X tokens. Start with default 60_000ms. Also emit a shadow decision metric for comparison.
Sanjay K.: I like shadow mode. We can run shadow decisions for 24h and compare false-rejects count. If shadow_rejects >> live_rejects, flip automatic grace.
Ellie (eng-platform): Ops concerns: extending burst allowance has cost/abuse implications. We should scope to per-org sampling and only for routes with low abuse score. Add a console flag per-org.
Adrian L.: Implementation sketch:
- enforcer: check counter_age = now - cached_ts
- if counter_age > grace && feature_flag(org, "enforcer_stale_grace") == true -> emit metric enforcer.shadow_decision{org, delta_tokens}, allow up to min(burst_left + grace_tokens, safe_limit)
- otherwise behave as today
Sanjay K.: Quick config snippet for FF service: 
```json
{"org_id":"org-123","flags":{"enforcer_stale_grace":true,"staleness_grace_ms":60000}}
```
Maya R.: We'll need dashboard changes: one panel for shadow_rejects / live_rejects, another for median counter_age per org, and a scatter of rejections vs ingestion-lag. Ellie can you add a mock?
Ellie (eng-platform): Yep, I'll add panels under Platform -> Quotas -> Enforcement; will include filters by route/model and a histogram of cached_ts age.
Kevin T.: Rollout plan: canary to 5 small orgs (internal test orgs) -> 5% production orgs with low SLO/low-cost -> 25% -> full. Keep shadow mode always on for initial 48h. Reconciliation worker to run every 60s to backfill any mismatches.
Maya R.: Testing: write a harness that injects kafka writeback delays and asserts enforcer decisions. Example harness commands: 
```bash
# simulate 30s writeback lag
make metering-harness LAG_MS=30000 TARGET_ORG=org-123
# run e2e load test for 10k rps for 60s
./scripts/loadgen --org org-123 --rate 10000 --duration 60
```
Adrian L.: One more thing: add a reconciliation reason code in billing ledger so we can decouple charge correctness from enforcement decisions. 
metering-bot: test-job metering_writeback_replay started for partition=4, target_lag=45s
Sanjay K.: Ok let's implement enforcer flag + shadow metrics this sprint. I'll own the enforcer change. Maya you own rollout runbook. Ellie will do dashboards. Adrian will spec reconciliation reason codes.
Maya R.: Thanks — I'll create a short playbook and post the canary checklist here when ready. :thumbsup:
Kevin T.: And add an alert: if shadow_rejects/live_rejects > 3x for > 15m, auto-pause strict enforcement and notify eng-platform oncall.
Maya R.: Good call. That should reduce user-impact while we validate.
